definitions.explanation: To have an opinion or belief about something. Often used with と{思|おも}う to express one's thoughts.
To have an emotional response or impression. そう{思|おも}う (I feel that way).
To anticipate or assume something. {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ると{思|おも}う (I think it will rain).

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}は{晴|は}れると{思|おも}います。
examples.english: I think it will be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{来|こ}ないと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I don't think he will come.
examples.notes: Negative inside the quote, not on {思|おも}う

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{暑|あつ}いと{思|おも}った。
examples.english: I thought it was hot today.

examples.japanese: あの{映画|えいが}は{面白|おもしろ}いと{思|おも}いますか。
examples.english: Do you think that movie is interesting?

examples.japanese: うれしいと{思|おも}っています。
{試験|しけん}は{難|むずか}しいと{思|おも}います。
examples.english: I expect the exam will be difficult.

examples.japanese: この{料理|りょうり}はおいしいと{思|おも}いませんか。
examples.english: Don't you think this dish is delicious?

examples.japanese: さびしいと{思|おも}うことがあります。
examples.english: There are times when I feel lonely.

examples.japanese: {田中|たなか}さんは{来|く}ると{思|おも}っていたのに、{来|こ}なかった。
examples.english: I expected Tanaka to come, but he didn't.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しいと{思|おも}っていましたが、{勉強|べんきょう}してみたら{楽|たの}しかったです。
examples.english: I thought Japanese would be difficult, but when I tried studying it, it was fun.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}のことを{思|おも}うと、{心|こころ}が{温|あたた}かくなります。
examples.english: When I think of her, my heart feels warm.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}は{混|こ}んでいると{思|おも}うので、{早|はや}く{出|で}ましょう。
examples.english: I expect the train will be crowded, so let's leave early.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}はとても{良|よ}いと{思|おも}うので、ぜひ{読|よ}んでみてください。
examples.english: I think this book is very good, so please try reading it.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). No pair verb. Pattern: 〜と{思|おも}う (think that ~) or Xを{思|おも}う (think of X).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing thought or opinion. {思|おも}っている = 'think/believe' (current opinion).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・〜と{思|おも}う (think that ~)
・どう{思|おも}う (what do you think?)
・そう{思|おも}う (I think so)
・〜と{思|おも}っている (believe/have the opinion that)

NOTE: Japanese often puts negatives inside the quote: {来|こ}ないと{思|おも}う rather than {来|く}ると{思|おも}わない.

Compare: {考|かんが}える implies more deliberate reasoning/consideration.
